sw19-r1.name: The one-sixteenth paragraph, rewritten after the near-miss steps were spent
sw19-r1.text: So a child today gets about one-sixteenth of the grown-ups that a child had when our brains evolved (Perry, 2023). If you often feel empty (the "Void"), that feeling is real, since you're living with a fraction of the people we're built to have around us. That loneliness is what the armor has been numbing, so once you've de-armored, going back to a lonely life will hurt more than it did with the armor on. So I'd find a tribe of people you're close to and see most days, or you'll end up putting the armor back on just to get through the loneliness.

pair2223-s2.name: The Anti-Breakthrough with the practice sentence, step 2 from its near miss
pair2223-s2.text:
The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): A brain stuck in alarm can often take in healing work for only a few seconds at a time, Perry finds. So for now we have to give up on the hour-long breakthrough that therapy aims for, since an hour spent working on the trauma itself overwhelms an armored nervous system more than it heals it. Instead, this protocol works in doses of a few seconds, which is what I mean by micro-dosing here.

In practice, that means 30 seconds of slow breathing to feel safe in your body, twenty times a day.
